annotations.text:
Direction A — built out.
One grid, always. Untagged recipes never sit on top of tagged ones.
Your tags are tiles above the grid: your icon, your colour, the covers of the recipes inside.
Tap a tile to filter in place. Tap the × to clear.
Manage a tag where you see it: "Edit tag" on the filtered header, or the + tile. Settings → Tags goes away.

One sheet replaces the list page and the editor page.
Same icons, colours and name toggle you liked — one tap closer.

Import: nothing lands untapped.
The site's categories come in as suggestions under the tags row.
Tap one to keep it. Leave it and it is never saved.
A suggestion that matches one of your tags wears that tag's colour and icon, so it never becomes a duplicate.

Direction B — the rail.
Cheapest: today's chips, one grid, filter in place. Manage from the ⋯ at the end of the rail.
Trade-off: a long rail hides tags off-screen, and tags stay small.

Direction C — a table of contents.
The cookbook opens as a list of your tags with counts. Tap one for its grid.
Most book-like. Trade-off: one more tap to every recipe.
